summary: CSV export splits multi-line tracehook fields, corrupting exported rows for embedded reports
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that CSV exports of dashboard report (embedded) have rows breaking across multiple lines. The 'tracehook' field — which can contain JSON with embedded newlines and HTML snippets — is being split into separate CSV rows, corrupting the CSV and causing downstream ETL failures for the customer.

Impact: Several scheduled exports for Summit Analytics failed validation in their ingestion pipeline; they were unable to reconcile daily usage and trace links for March 10-12. Customer considers this a data-loss/blocking billing reconciliation issue.

Environment: prod exports for org ID org-85312 (Summit Analytics), export service running in us-east, CSV generation executed via exporter job schedule (daily at 02:00 UTC).

Steps to reproduce:
1) In Console -> Reports -> Scheduled Exports, select "Usage + Tracehook CSV" with default output rows that include the 'tracehook' column.
2) Trigger ad-hoc export for org-85312 or download last successful run.
3) Open CSV in a strict CSV parser (Python csv.reader or pandas.read_csv) and observe parser errors or unexpected record counts.
4) Look for rows where a single exported record corresponds to multiple physical lines in the file; inspect the 'tracehook' column content for unescaped line breaks.

Observed behavior: The CSV file contains physically broken rows (line breaks inside fields are not properly quoted or normalized), causing file to have more rows than expected; when the CSV is parsed, records shift and subsequent columns appear in wrong rows.

Expected behavior: Fields that contain newlines should be properly quoted and escaped per RFC4180, or newline-normalized consistently so CSV parsers do not split records incorrectly.
comments: 2026-03-12 09:17 - Summit Analytics (customer): We pulled today's scheduled CSV and our ingestion failed with 'parser error: expected 12 columns, found 1' for multiple files. This started on 2026-03-10. Please advise — it's blocking billing reconciliation.

2026-03-12 09:45 - Support (Ava Martinez): Thanks for the report. We're investigating. Can you attach the failing CSV (or a redacted sample) and the ingestion error? Also confirm whether this export was previously successful for you.
2026-03-12 10:03 - Summit Analytics: Uploaded sample file to secure share (link provided). Exports were previously fine, stopped failing after retention compaction last week per their note.

2026-03-12 11:22 - Support (Ava): We reproduced the issue locally with a synthetic tracehook containing embedded \n and HTML. Opening the CSV in pandas triggers the exact parser error. Triage to Eng/Exporting team and SRE. Assigned to Ravi.

2026-03-12 14:10 - Eng (Ravi Patel): Initial hypothesis: a recent normalization change in exporter introduced CRLF conversion plus a bug skipping quoting for fields >16KB. Looking at exporter logs for job run 2026-03-12-02:00 — saw exporter v2.14.0 (deployed 2026-03-09) in the stack trace.

2026-03-12 16:30 - SRE (Liam Chen): Confirmed that export job restarted during indexer compaction on 2026-03-09 02:01. There were transient retries and a deploy (PR 7b2f9d1) to the exporter service pushed 2026-03-09 03:00 UTC. Pinning those events for root cause timeline.

2026-03-13 08:05 - Eng (Ravi): Added hotfix branch to ensure proper quoting of newline-containing fields and added unit tests. Preparing hotfix roll. Notifying customer of temporary workaround (download JSON export and reformat).

2026-03-14 02:20 - Support (Ava): Hotfix deployed to prod (exporter v2.14.1). Re-ran customer's failed exports for March 10-12; upload links provided in secure share. Customer confirmed that CSVs now parse correctly in their pipeline.
investigation: Reproduced locally: created tracehook payload with multi-line JSON and HTML, ran exporter v2.14.0 -> CSV produced unquoted newlines leading to broken rows.
SRE timeline: indexer compaction and exporter service restart occurred 2026-03-09 02:00-03:15 UTC; exporter v2.14.0 deployed 2026-03-09 03:00 (PR 7b2f9d1).

Code inspection: exporter change 'normalize_newlines' (commit 7b2f9d1) replaced \n with OS-native line ending and then wrote rows without forcing quoting for large fields; python csv.writer default quoting strategy was ALREADY set but a conditional bypass for large fields avoided quoting.

Root cause: regression in exporter -- a conditional short-circuit skip (intended for performance) bypassed csv.QUOTE_MINIMAL for fields above 16KB after newline normalization. Fields containing embedded newlines were therefore written raw, producing physical line breaks in file.

Risk assessment: affects scheduled CSV exports which include tracehook/content columns; impact surface limited to exports that contain large multi-line fields (common for embedded tracehooks). No ingestion/consumer-side application code changes required, but customers' downstream ETL can fail.
Related: observed similar symptom in SUP-61234 (saved_query_timespan_timeout_trace_404) but that ticket is not root cause; linked for context.
Mitigation attempted: advised customer to use JSON export (which serializes fields safely) as immediate workaround.
Test coverage gap found: exporter lacked unit tests for multi-line field quoting and large-field paths.
resolution: Hotfix deployed: exporter v2.14.1 reverted the short-circuit that bypassed quoting and explicitly uses csv.QUOTE_ALL for fields containing newlines. Deployed to prod 2026-03-14 01:40 UTC.

Customer impact remediation: Re-ran scheduled exports for Summit Analytics for 2026-03-10 through 2026-03-12 and uploaded fixed CSVs to the customer's secure share. Customer confirmed ingestion success on 2026-03-14 03:10 UTC.
Workaround provided: If customers see failures before fix, use JSON export or pipe CSV through a preprocessor that re-quotes multiline fields (instructions provided in support reply).

Follow-up tasks created: INT-901745 (add exporter unit tests for multi-line/large-field quoting), INT-901746 (audit scheduled deployments during indexer compaction windows), and ENG-PR-3490 (add integration test against customer's ingestion pipeline in CI).
Postmortem planned: Confluence page created and assigned to Exporting team. Postmortem due by 2026-03-20.
Status: Customer issue resolved; monitoring exports for 48 hours across affected orgs. Will update ticket to 'Resolved' after 48h with no regressions.
